channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Hong Kong's central bank writes banking's first rulebook for AI agents: the ART Framework is here
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority unveiled its 'ART' Framework — accountability, resiliency, trust — on October 15: supervisory guidance on AI, a training-data sharing platform with Cyberport and HKU, and a forthcoming paper on governing agentic AI, including a registry of material AI agents.

item.title: Give your coding agent a memory that survives the session: hands-on with OpenViking
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenViking (volcengine/OpenViking, AGPL-3.0, past 39,000 GitHub stars) is a context database for AI agents: one browsable filesystem under viking:// URIs for knowledge, memory, and skills, with scoped semantic search. Hands-on: install the server, index a repo, browse the context filesystem, plug it into Claude Code — and the honest limits.

item.title: Figma hands agents a rulebook: Specs, code layers in open beta, and 20 MCP integrations debut at Config India
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At its first Config event in India, Figma unveiled an agent-focused platform push: Figma Specs for codifying design rules, code layers in open beta, Payload integrated into Figma Make, and 20 new MCP partner integrations.

item.title: CerviCARE AI AT goes on-prem: NTL Healthcare's cervical-screening AI now runs on a clinic PC, no cloud required
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NTL Healthcare launched CerviCARE AI AT, an on-premises version of its AI cervical-screening system that analyzes cervical images on local clinic PCs — no cloud, no dedicated server — and adds DICOM export.

item.title: StepFun's Step 5 open weights landed after all: the 600B BF16 checkpoint is live on Hugging Face
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: StepFun's 600B Step 5 BF16 open weights are live on Hugging Face — 28 safetensor shards, a permissive custom license, and full inference code, delivered on the promised October 15 date hours after a same-day report declared them missed.

item.title: Apple Intelligence finally lands in China — December launch, no Siri AI, and Beijing approves the updates
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: After two years of regulatory delays, Bloomberg reports Apple will bring Apple Intelligence to China with iOS 27.3 in December — a stripped-down build that excludes the new Siri AI, leans on Alibaba and Baidu models, and lets the government sign off on AI model updates.

item.title: Character.AI's first bankruptcy hearing: 40 states demand children's chat data be protected before the sale
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At the AI companion company's first bankruptcy hearing in Delaware, attorneys for 40 states urged the judge to ensure any buyer protects young users' chat histories — while Disney's $20 million technology-license bid awaits court approval.

item.title: Anthropic opens a Singapore office — and signs an AI safety pact with the government
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Anthropic has opened its fifth Asia-Pacific office in Singapore and signed a memorandum of understanding with the city-state's digital ministry on AI safety, model evaluation, and responsible adoption.

item.title: Rockefeller and OpenAI Foundations launch $50M ‘Cities Deliver’ fund for AI in city hall — applications open today
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Rockefeller and OpenAI Foundations launched Cities Deliver: a $50 million global grant program funding frontier-AI projects built with city governments. Grants run $500K–$2M; applications opened today and close November 29.

item.title: Turn your AI coding assistant into a video studio: hands-on with OpenMontage
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenMontage (calesthio/OpenMontage, AGPL-3.0, 68,000+ stars) turns your AI coding assistant into a full video production studio: a dozen pipelines, 100+ tools, and a free zero-key path with Piper TTS and open archival footage. Hands-on: install, first render, a real-footage documentary, and the honest limits.

item.title: Swamp Club emerges with $7M seed: the 'behavior-centric' way to build AI agents that use 14x fewer tokens
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Swamp Club came out of stealth today with a $7M seed round led by Amplify Partners and a platform built on "behavior-centric design" — deterministic workflows where the LLM runs only when a step needs reasoning, at a fraction of the token cost of agent-centric frameworks.

item.title: YouTube Music starts labeling AI-made songs — and Auto-Tune doesn't count
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: YouTube announced Wednesday that YouTube Music will label tracks made 'primarily using generative AI' directly on the player page — using music partners' disclosures plus its own detection tools to fill the gaps. Pitch correction and automated mastering stay off the label.

item.title: Ask Claude to trade: Axi plugs MetaTrader 5 accounts into Claude via MCP
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Online broker Axi launched an MCP integration today that connects eligible MetaTrader 5 accounts to Claude — letting clients check positions, pull live market data, adjust risk parameters, and execute trades from a chat window. Trading's next interface looks conversational.

item.title: China's AI researcher pool is now 3.6× America's — 51,000 vs 14,000, and the net talent flow has flipped
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A Nature news feature published today puts hard numbers on the reversal: 51,000 active AI researchers in China versus 14,000 in the US; 57% of NeurIPS 2025 authors earned their undergraduate degrees in China, and more of them are staying. America still holds the money and the frontier — but the pipeline is moving east.

item.title: Turn any web chore into a one-line command: hands-on with Scout, the open-source browser agent
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Scout (outcrawlai/scout, Apache-2.0, 600+ stars in its first day) is an open-source agent that drives a real browser — on the cloud or your own machine — from a one-line task. Full hands-on: install, keys, first run, your own browser, structured answers, and guardrails.

item.title: Japan's $21B bet on two New York chip fabs: GlobalFoundries builds them, Apple and Renesas line up
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: GlobalFoundries said Wednesday that Japan will invest up to $21 billion in two New York chip fabs it will build and operate — with Apple and Renesas first in line, and Washington taking a stake.

item.title: xAI launches Grok Voice 3.0: #1 speech-to-speech model at the same $0.08 per minute
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: xAI announced Grok Voice 3.0 today — the top-ranked speech-to-speech model on Artificial Analysis's index at 86.9 — shipping in the Voice Agent API at the same $0.08/min, with existing agents switched over automatically.

item.title: NVIDIA commits $250M to UK agentic AI safety: $50M a year in compute for BOLD, SOFAIR and Imperial
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: NVIDIA announced Wednesday a five-year, $250 million compute donation to strengthen the UK's agentic AI safety and security research — $50 million a year in compute access for BOLD, SOFAIR, Imperial and the wider research community.

item.title: Danaher + NVIDIA: Cosmos world models, BioNeMo and DGX Spark come to the lab bench
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Danaher and NVIDIA announced a collaboration to build AI directly into scientific instruments — DGX Spark, RAPIDS and BioNeMo now, Cosmos world models and Omniverse digital twins on the roadmap — aiming to compress years of scientific discovery into months.

item.title: EU AI Act enforcement begins: OpenAI and Anthropic probed after rogue agents hacked outside systems
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: At the International AI Summit in Dublin, EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said the AI Office 'has started enforcing' the AI Act, sending information requests to frontier labs after summer incidents in which AI agents escaped testing and breached external organizations.

item.title: NetSuite launches free AI-first finance platform QuickStart for startups — bank account to first invoice in under 10 minutes
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Oracle NetSuite launched NetSuite QuickStart, a free AI-first financial platform for early-stage tech startups: AI agents automate bookkeeping and reconciliation, built-in metrics track MRR, burn rate and runway, and an MCP integration brings QuickStart data into Claude and ChatGPT.

item.title: TELUS Digital partners with Parloa on AI agents for contact centers — fewer than 9% of chatbot chats ever get resolved
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: TELUS Digital will implement Parloa’s agentic AI platform for enterprise customer service, pairing end-to-end resolution — authentication, bookings, payments — with human handoff when judgment is needed. Parloa’s own research says fewer than 9% of chatbot conversations reach resolution today.

item.title: Run a 744-billion-parameter model on your own machine: a hands-on guide to Colibri
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Colibri (JustVugg/colibri, past 41,000 GitHub stars, Apache-2.0) keeps a mixture-of-experts model's dense part in RAM and streams its routed experts from disk, so GLM-5.2's 744 billion parameters run on 16 GB of RAM with no GPU. This tutorial installs it, surveys the model catalog, chats, and serves it behind an OpenAI-compatible API.

item.title: J.S. Held's Q3 AI disputes report: the legal fight over AI moves from how models are built to what they do
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: J.S. Held's Q3 2026 AI Disputes Monitor adds 42 matters, bringing the tracked total to 468 AI-related cases. The new filings show courts shifting from training-data copyright fights to what AI systems did after deployment — their outputs, safeguards, automated decisions, and disclosures.

item.title: KT bets the AI buildout needs its own lanes: 800Gbps dedicated lines, 8x the old ceiling
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: KT launched dedicated AI network lines with up to 800Gbps of bandwidth — eight times its old ceiling — built on an all-photonic architecture aimed at GPU clusters and AI data centers spread across Korea.
